title: Variationally Optimized Imaginary-time Polynomial Filters for Ground State Projection
authors: Bahman Seifi, Ibsal Assi, J. P. F. LeBlanc
abstract: In this work, we develop a variational imaginary-time evolution (ITE) framework based on polynomial filtering, derived from an operator-level action principle, which yields an optimized non-unitary projector expressed as a polynomial in the Hamiltonian. Starting from a single-ancilla, first-order imaginary-time update defined by a Taylor expansion and Trotter-Suzuki (TS) decompositions, we show that replacing these approximations with alternative variational formulas substantially improves both accuracy and stability at larger time steps, leading to up to an order-of-magnitude enhancement in the final success probability. We further derive rigorous error bounds that depend only on static properties of the Hamiltonian, providing practical guidance for selecting the simulation time step. Benchmarks on the transverse-field Ising model demonstrate faster convergence to the ground-state energy and improved robustness compared to standard TS--Taylor ITE, highlighting variational polynomial filtering as a practical route to higher-fidelity ground-state preparation on near-term quantum devices.
summary: This paper introduces a variational imaginary-time evolution (ITE) framework using polynomial filtering to project quantum states onto their ground state. By optimizing the evolution parameters variationally, the method overcomes the accuracy and stability limitations of standard Trotter-Suzuki or Taylor approximations. Benchmarking on the Ising model shows this approach provides higher fidelity and robustness for quantum simulation on current hardware.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the ground state of a quantum many-body system by implementing imaginary-time evolution (ITE).
main_result: The proposed variational polynomial filtering framework significantly improves the accuracy and stability of ground-state projection compared to standard Trotter-Suzuki or Taylor approximations, especially for larger time steps.
method: The authors develop an action-based variational approach (ABVA) to optimize the parameters in the imaginary-time evolution operator, replacing fixed-coefficient approximations with variational formulas.
model_or_system: The methodology is benchmarked on the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model (QIM), which serves as the quantum many-body system Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Success probability, convergence rate to the ground-state energy, and derived error bounds.
important_parameters: Imaginary time step ($	au$ or $\delta	au$), Hamiltonian parameters ($J, h_x, h_z$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The process relies on postselection on the desired measurement outcome, inducing an effective non-unitary transformation, and the initial state must have non-zero overlap with the ground state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ancilla-assisted implementation of ITE, comparing energy evolution for standard TS-Taylor methods against the optimized variational approach for the QIM.
paper_structure: The paper develops the ITE framework, details the variational optimization (ABVA/ABVPA) for the projector, derives rigorous error bounds based on static Hamiltonian properties, and validates the method using the QIM benchmark.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the resource limitations and accuracy bottlenecks in simulating ground states on near-term quantum devices by providing a more robust, variational circuit implementation for ITE.
